title: Why demeanor is a poor guide to lying
figureCaption: Figure 33.4: Beliefs about behavioral “tells” exceed the observed associations for several behaviors. Positive values indicate more of a behavior during deception, observed or believed according to the series. Across nine observed correlations, the largest absolute value is .19; several estimates are heterogeneous. Seven pairs of belief estimates are available, with none reported for nodding or hand movements. Sporer and Schwandt (2007, Figure 1) report the observed associations; their belief estimates came from Zuckerman et al. (1981) and Köhnken (1988).
